name: Shopwatch
description: Cycle-time measurement for the shop floor, read in units per hour. The screen is the floor as it is walked: cells, the machines standing in each, and on every machine the tool layouts it is set up to run — the tooling for one operation, with a number of its own and the pockets the watch times. One layout can be run on several machines, and every cycle stays with the machine it was taken on, so their rates stay apart. Machines set on the same operation run at once, so their rates add and the operation's effective cycle falls: that is what the value stream is paced by, along with the slowest step it names. Cutting time is measured at the machine rather than typed, the layout's cycle is charted across its tools, a part's route across the cells is drawn as a value stream map, and both print — one tool layout to a page. CSV in and out, a row group per machine.
